clue.text: Held back, being rather unsociable

blocks.note: first meaning: kept aside or booked for later use
second meaning: shy, inclined to keep to oneself

explanation.surface: Someone hangs back at a party because they are not much of a mixer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means set aside for later, as with a booked table, and also describes a quiet, standoffish temperament.

clue.text: Salad food sustaining an artistic person?

indicators.note: in a down answer, what sustains another holds it up from underneath, so it is written second

blocks.note: a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
dishes are items of food served at a meal

explanation.surface: A light meal of leaves keeps a starving painter going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salad food' reads as a single phrase, but only Salad defines; food is the second piece, standing under the artist in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: These crisp red roots are sliced into green salads, so they are typical salad ingredients.

clue.text: Arranging a loan isn't a bloomer

indicators.note: arranging means putting into a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Setting up a bank loan is not a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, but here it is literally something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton lavender is a small shrub with yellow button flowers, so it is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Give up and watch when upset

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom

blocks.note: a timer is a device that watches the clock, as a stopwatch does

explanation.surface: Someone quits and keeps an eye on things when distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: One old sense of the verb is to surrender or relinquish, as in forgoing a claim or a penalty.

clue.text: He demands payment from a one-time player

blocks.note: ex means former
an actor plays a part

explanation.surface: A man asks a former performer to pay up.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a sum is to insist on it being paid, so one who exacts is a collector insisting on money owed.

clue.text: The depths reached by an asinine craftsman?

blocks.note: first meaning: the lowest point of something
second meaning: the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream who is given a donkey's head

explanation.surface: Someone has sunk as low as possible, helped down by a foolish tradesman.
explanation.walkthrough: Asinine usually means stupid, but here it is literal: Shakespeare's weaver is transformed so that he wears an ass's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the lowest point or seabed, and it is also the name of Shakespeare's weaver, a working craftsman.

clue.text: Working man getting his knife into someone

definitions.text: man getting his knife into someone

blocks.note: first meaning: functioning, as a machine in use is

blocks.clueFragment: man getting his knife into someone
blocks.note: second meaning: what a surgeon does when he cuts open a patient

explanation.walkthrough: Getting your knife into someone usually means attacking them; here the knife is a scalpel, and the noun matches the first sense through 'in ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means functioning, as in a machine in use, and a surgical procedure in which a doctor cuts into a patient.

clue.text: A pupil in this colour might well appear smart

indicators.note: the clue says the answer with a pupil put in would give another word, so taking that pupil out goes backwards

blocks.note: to smart is to sting or prickle
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plates

explanation.surface: A student dressed in this shade would look very well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works in reverse: put a learner into the answer and you get a word for smart, so remove that letter from the stinging word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour, a faint shade, so it can stand for a hue.

clue.text: Very small record

blocks.note: first meaning: tiny, pronounced with a long u
second meaning: to write up the official notes of a meeting

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means tiny, and as a verb it means to take down the formal notes of a committee meeting.

clue.text: Bit of a swine to get through such a collection of food!

blocks.note: ham is meat from a pig's thigh
per means by way of or through, as in per post

explanation.surface: A gift basket so stuffed with pork that it is hard work to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description, since a Christmas basket often holds a ham to work through.
explanation.definitionFit: This lidded wicker basket packed with food is the classic picnic or Christmas gift box of provisions.

clue.text: Stuff taken from the ground should be put back

indicators.note: putting something back here means writing the word in the opposite direction

blocks.note: dug out, as coal or ore is

explanation.surface: Material dug out of the earth ought to be returned to where it came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuff is an old word for woven fabric, not a verb or general clutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is a traditional term for cloth, and this sturdy cotton twill used for jeans is one such fabric.

clue.text: Old Greek man possibly holding contest over

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters given could be arranged some other way
one piece holds the next inside it, wrapping around it

blocks.note: the letters of man rearranged
a game is a contest or match
on can mean over or upon, as a lid sits on a pot

explanation.surface: A man from ancient Greece may have been the one presiding over the games.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled man splits open after its first letter to take in the contest, and the final two letters come last.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Mycenae who led the Greek army against Troy is a figure from ancient Greek legend.

clue.text: Brief break for one of the baseball team

blocks.note: brief means short in duration
a stop is a pause or break

explanation.surface: A baseball player gets a short rest between innings.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fielding position between second and third base, so its player is a member of a baseball side.

clue.text: Some faith-healer, talkative and watchful

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their run of letters is wanted

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A chatty faith-healer who keeps a careful eye on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone paying close attention and quick to notice danger or change.

clue.text: He turns out to be the winner by a point

blocks.note: east, one of the compass points
a victor is the one who wins

explanation.surface: A man proves to have won by the narrowest margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He turns out to be' reads as a single phrase, but the definition stops at 'turns out', meaning throws out of a home; 'by' simply puts the point beside the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who evicts tenants physically turns them out of the property, so he is someone who turns people out.

clue.text: Chance it perhaps if over 50 — it's quite practical

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters may be found in some other arrangement

blocks.note: the letters as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A gambler is urged to take a risk once past fifty, as it is a sensible move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' here just means in addition, so the numeral joins the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical knowledge concerns applied skills and methods rather than theory, so it is the practical kind.

clue.text: Fruit is set in wet weather

indicators.note: something set in another thing is placed inside it

blocks.note: rain is wet weather
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fruit is planted while it is pouring outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The small word goes inside the weather word, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a kind of fruit, used in baking and eaten as a snack.

clue.text: A way article may be squeezed in between right now

indicators.note: squeezing something in means pressing it inside something else

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an is the indefinite article
inter is the Latin for between

explanation.surface: A route and an article are crammed into a gap at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The road and the article join first, then sit inside the Latin word, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This old legal adverb means immediately, without delay, so it matches at this very moment.

clue.text: Step over a weapon, knowing it could gain one access

blocks.note: a pas is a step in ballet
a sword is a weapon

explanation.surface: Stepping across a sword lying on the floor, someone knows it gets them in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'over' puts the step above the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word or phrase lets the person who knows it through a door or into a computer system.

clue.text: Dressing right as part of the service

blocks.note: a sauce dresses food
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The correct dressing is brought out as part of a restaurant's table service.
explanation.walkthrough: Service suggests waiting at table, but it means a matching set of crockery, as in a tea service.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea or dinner service is a set of matching crockery, and this small dish for a cup is one item in it.

clue.text: Material assistance will be rewarded

blocks.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
aid is help

explanation.surface: Practical help given to someone will be returned in kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Material looks like an adjective meaning substantial, but it is a noun for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To be repaid is to be paid back or recompensed for what one gave, the same as being rewarded.

clue.text: Nobody can recall being affected by it

definitions.text: Nobody can recall being affected by it

blocks.clueFragment: Nobody can recall being affected by it
blocks.note: surface reading: a thing so minor or so long ago that no one remembers it touching them
setter's reading: the condition itself wipes the memory, so anyone who has it cannot recall anything

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a forgotten event nobody experienced; in fact it is the affliction that destroys the ability to remember.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical condition is loss of memory, so sufferers literally cannot remember things, including the illness.

clue.text: Marshal mounted gunners on the firing area

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounted means raised up, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
a firing range is where shooting is practised

explanation.surface: A military officer on horseback leads artillerymen on to the shooting ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshal looks like a noun for an officer, but it is a verb meaning to put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal troops or facts is to set them out in order, which is exactly what to arrange means.

clue.text: Hector could be Sarah's undoing

indicators.note: undoing something takes it apart, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the letters of the name, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man called Hector might be the one who ruins Sarah.
explanation.walkthrough: Hector looks like a man's name, but it is a verb meaning to bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or nag someone aggressively, which is to pester and torment them.

clue.text: An imprisoning for offering protection

indicators.note: a prison holds its inmate inside, so one word encloses the next

blocks.note: taken as written
pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone jailed in exchange for protection, like a gangland deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The short word opens after its first letter to take in the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: This garment is tied over clothes to keep them clean while cooking, so it acts as a protective covering.

clue.text: Loot for the sovereign in general

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the coin goes within the word for general

blocks.note: rife means widespread or general, as an illness rife in a town
a sovereign was a pound coin, and L (from libra) is the pound sign

explanation.surface: Plunder is seized on behalf of the monarch by an army commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Sovereign and general both look like people of rank, but one is an old gold pound coin and the other means widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack and rob it, so as a verb it means to plunder or loot.

clue.text: Workers following political leader they support

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
one part comes after the other, so the second piece goes first

blocks.note: the first letter of political
artisans are skilled manual workers

explanation.surface: Workers fall in behind the party leader whom they back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Political leader' suggests a person at the head of a party, but it only supplies an initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisans are committed adherents of a cause or party, people who back it, so the plural noun matches those who support.

clue.text: Problem children

blocks.note: first meaning: a matter of concern or dispute
second meaning: offspring, as in died without legal heirs

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests troublesome kids; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a disputed point or difficulty, and in legal language it means a person's offspring or descendants.

clue.text: Love may be seen as a pathological condition!

blocks.note: first meaning: fondness or warm feeling
second meaning: a medical term for a disease affecting part of the body

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark jokes that love is a sickness; in medicine the word really does mean a disorder of an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tender fondness, and doctors use it for a disease or disorder, as in an affection of the lungs.

clue.text: Tote's mistake causes argument

indicators.note: a mistake implies things have gone wrong, so the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: the letters of the word, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An error by the betting machine starts a row at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tote is the British state-run betting system at racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or heated quarrel, the same as an argument.

clue.text: Getting fish into a pen is very hard

indicators.note: getting one thing into another means placing it inside

blocks.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Catching a fish and putting it into an enclosure is a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen looks like a writing tool, but it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the metal itself, something with this quality is unyielding and tough, extremely hard in manner or substance.

clue.text: Submitted when the umpire made a wrong decision

blocks.note: a ref, short for referee, is an umpire
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A complaint is lodged after the match official gets a call wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a matter on to someone else for a decision is to hand it over, so the past tense matches submitted.
